newsitem.title: USA: Lower chicken prices push U.S. farm price index down.
newsitem.headline: Lower chicken prices push U.S. farm price index down.

text.p: Lower prices for chickens, eggs, tomatoes and strawberries pushed the farm price index down by 0.9 percent for April, the Agriculture Department said Wednesday.
The index, a gauge of prices paid to farmers for their crops and livestock, had an April reading of 106, down 0.9 percent from March, and 1.9 percent lower than a year ago.

The April broiler price, at 37.1 cents per pound, was down 0.9 cents from March, while market eggs dropped 7.3 cents to 53.2 cents per dozen in April. The department said broiler and egg supplies continue to be large and demand has eased.
Prices for tomatoes tumbled to $28.00 per 100 pounds from $58.00 in March and strawberry prices nearly halved to 47.5 cents per pound, the department said in its monthly report.
These decreases were offset by price gains for hogs and wheat in April, the department said.
It said hog prices climbed $3.90 to average $53.30 per 100 pounds in April, largely due to booming exports in the wake of hog disease outbreaks in Europe and Asia.
Wheat prices rose 23 cents to average $4.16 per bushel. Corn prices were unchanged at $2.79 per bushel in April.

Cattle prices averaged $65.00 in April, 20 cents higher than in March. The department said fast food specials and lower slaughter weights continued to support prices despite large live cattle supplies.
Soybeans prices rose 6 cents from March to average $8.03 per bushel in April, reflecting tight supplies.
The all-milk price was flat during April at an average $13.50 per 100 pounds, but was 40 cents below last year, the department said.
